input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The rewritten loop removes only each parameter's primary opts from the candidate help names and no longer removes its secondary_opts, dropping a step the replaced set-based code performed.
- failure path: A command with context help_option_names ['-h', '--help'] and an option declared as '--hint/-h' keeps -h as a help name, so the generated help option and the user's option both claim -h and `cmd -h` prints help instead of setting the flag the author declared.

Reviewer finding
- description: The loop no longer removes a parameter's secondary_opts from the help option names, so a help name that is also a secondary option of another parameter (e.g. a flag declared as "--x/-h") is now kept as a help name.
- rationale: Trigger: a command has a parameter whose secondary_opts includes a default help name such as "-h". Before this change that name was removed from the help names, so no conflict arose. After the change, the help option keeps "-h" as well, so the name is claimed twice and the parser or help behavior can conflict or resolve to the wrong option. Impact: the user may see a conflicting-option error or have "-h" trigger help instead of the intended flag. I am not certain the removal was intended, which is why confidence is moderate.
critique: The finding pins down the same mechanism as the label: the rewritten loop no longer removes secondary_opts from the help names. It also gives the same failure: a flag declared like '--x/-h' keeps -h as a help name, so `-h` is claimed twice and can trigger help instead of the flag.
